newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Dutch vow support for Philippine peace efforts.
newsitem.headline: Dutch vow support for Philippine peace efforts.

text.p: Dutch Prime Minister Wim Kok on Thursday pledged the Netherlands' continued support for Philippine efforts to negotiate an end to a 27-year Marxist insurgency.

Kok arrived in Manila for an overnight visit and held talks with President Fidel Ramos on issues ranging from economic ties to human rights and cooperation in the fight against sexual exploitation of children.
The Netherlands has hosted several rounds of talks between a Philippine government panel and Filipino Marxist exiles living in the Dutch city of Utrecht.

"We in the Netherlands will be very glad if in one way or the other we can facilitate the process of continuing the peace talks in order to come to fruitful results," Kok told a news conference after his talks with Ramos.
Manila last month reached a peace deal with Moslem separatist rebels, ending a 24-year revolt by Moslem separatists in the southern Philippines. The talks were brokered by Islamic nations.
Kok expressed hope that a five-year prison sentence handed down last month by a Dutch court to a Dutchman for sex offenses against young girls in the Philippines would help stamp out paedophilia.
The Dutch court action "is a considerable step forward...to make an end to this problem," Kok said.
The two sides signed several official agreements and business deals worth a combined $19 million covering energy, nutrition, the environment and insurance.
In two of the deals, Aegon NV and ING Insurance, an arm of financial services giant ING Group, won licences to start life insurance businesses in the Philippines.
